## Glossary

**app-events**  
Class: the emitAppEvent side-effect bus, makeAppEvent handlers, their email/WebSocket/observe handoffs and commit deferral.

**AppEvent**  
Model recording emitted events (upserted by envelope id) with actor, source and payload; diagnostic, not read back by code.

**AppEventName**  
Typed union of event names, declared with their payloads and registrations in apps/api/src/appEvents/handlers/index.ts.

**auditActorContext**  
Async-scope actor provenance that emitAppEvent copies onto the event envelope.

**circuit breaker**  
A subscription auto-disables (isActive = false) after 5 consecutive failed events.

**db.onCommit**  
Defers a callback until the surrounding transaction commits; emitAppEvent and the webhook hook use it.

**db.parallel**  
Runs tasks in their own database-client / data-modeling async scopes; with resolution allSettled each may fail alone and the failures are thrown after settlement.

**EmailHandoff**  
{ template, data } returned by a handler's email selector; recipients and sender come from the email registry, never to/cc/bcc on the handoff.

**emitAppEvent**  
emitAppEvent(name, data): builds the actor envelope and runs the registered handler, after commit when inside db.txn().

**HOOK_IGNORE_FIELDS**  
Shared ignore registry: fields excluded from webhook payloads, stripped from audit diffs and treated as no-op updates; composes encrypted and ordered-list fields.

**makeAppEvent**  
Defines an event handler { email, websocket, cb } whose tasks run isolated with allSettled and aggregated failures.

**observeRegistry**  
Broadcasts every envelope to the structured log and database-client / data-modeling adapters; best-effort, not a retry queue; no per-handler observe selector.

**poisoned record**  
On an integration subscription, a record with 3 rejections (400/422) since its last success while another record delivered gets IntegrationRecord.poisonedAt set; later deliveries skip it (services in adapters-integrations).

**sendWebhook**  
Job handler delivering one event to one subscription: sign, POST, record, retry; skips poisoned records before signing.

**streamAppend**  
Builds a stream handoff from a shared STREAM_DEFINITIONS entry, its params, an op and a typed payload; upsert rows come from routeRow.

**validateWebhookUrl**  
Rejects unsafe user-supplied target URLs (private addresses; relaxed in non-enforced envs); isPrivateAddress and hostnameOf are its building blocks.

**webhookDelivery**  
The after-commit db hook that finds a model's active subscriptions and enqueues one sendWebhook job per subscription.

**webhookEnabledModels**  
Registry of models whose mutations fire outbound webhooks (currently CustomerRef).

**WebhookEvent**  
One delivery attempt: status (pending/sent/failed), payload, HTTP status and response; cleaned after 90 days.

**webhookModelSubscribers**  
Inverse of webhookOwnerAllowedModels: from a changed model to the owner kinds that may receive it.

**webhookOwnerAllowedModels**  
Declares which models each owner kind (User, Organization, Space) may subscribe to; edit here to permit a new subscription.

**webhookRelatedModels**  
Maps a model to related records (FlexibleRef) whose changes fire its webhooks.

**webhooks**  
Class: outbound webhooks: subscriptions, signed delivery jobs, delivery history, URL safety, circuit breaker.

**WebhookSubscription**  
A User/Organization/Space-owned URL subscribed to a WebhookModel, unique per owner, model and url, with isActive and an optional integrationId.

**webhookUrlSchema**  
Zod wrapper over validateWebhookUrl for subscription request bodies.

**WSHandoff**  
WebSocket handoff: kind 'channels' or 'users' with a message (refetch hints), or kind 'stream' with an append built by streamAppend.

**x-webhook-signature**  
Base64 RSA-SHA256 signature of the timestamped body; receivers verify with the public key at /webhookSubscription/info.

## 1. What this Warden covers

How a business write reaches the outside world: typed app events whose handlers fan out to email, WebSocket, observation and callbacks after commit, and signed outbound webhooks that the mutation hook system fires for enabled models and delivers through jobs.

## 2. The domain

App events are the only way business logic triggers a side effect. A write path calls emitAppEvent(name, data); the name and payload type are declared in apps/api/src/appEvents/handlers/index.ts (AppEventName) and the handler is built with makeAppEvent({ email, websocket, cb }). emitAppEvent wraps the data in a UUIDv7 envelope with the actor from auditActorContext and, inside db.txn(), defers execution with db.onCommit; outside a transaction the handler runs at once. makeAppEvent runs observation, each handoff and each callback isolated through db.parallel(…, allSettled), so one failure does not cancel its siblings. Email handoffs (template + data) go to the sendEmail planner job; WebSocket handoffs go through sendToChannel/sendToUser or, for data streams, an append built with streamAppend and routeRow, never a hand-built { kind: 'stream' } object; the observe registry always receives the whole envelope and upserts AppEvent best-effort. Heavy or retryable work is enqueued from a cb, never done inline, and nothing synchronous calls an external service from a request. Inquiry-specific events live under modules/inquiry/handlers/<type>/appEvents.ts and reuse the shared handoff contracts.

Webhooks are driven by the mutation hook system, not by app events: a commit on a model in webhookEnabledModels (or a child listed in webhookRelatedModels) makes the webhookDelivery hook enqueue one sendWebhook job per active WebhookSubscription. The job signs the timestamped body with RSA-SHA256 (x-webhook-signature, public key at /webhookSubscription/info), delivers it, records a WebhookEvent, retries with backoff, and auto-disables the subscription after 5 consecutive failures (the circuit breaker). On a subscription with an integrationId, one record the receiver keeps rejecting with 400/422 is poisoned instead of tripping the circuit; the Integration and IntegrationRecord models and the poisonIntegrationRecord / isIntegrationRecordPoisoned services that do this live in the `adapters-integrations` region. Who may subscribe to what is declared in webhookOwnerAllowedModels (webhookModelSubscribers is its inverse); target URLs pass validateWebhookUrl (outside zod) or webhookUrlSchema (in request bodies), and registerWebhookSubscriptionUrlHook checks every URL write. HOOK_IGNORE_FIELDS is the shared ignore registry: fields listed there are left out of webhook payloads, stripped from audit diffs and treated as no-op updates, and it composes encrypted and ordered-list fields automatically.

Not here: adapter modules, owner Integrations, IntegrationRecords and object storage (`adapters-integrations`: makeAdapterRouter, makeBroadcastRegistry, findOwnedIntegration, storage, createS3Client); the email planner and delivery rules (email-delivery) and templates (email-templates); the WebSocket connection and stream machinery itself (ws-connections, ws-streams: sendToChannel, sendToUser, streamAppend, refetch, routeRow); the db hook registry and onCommit internals (mutation-hooks / database-client / data-modeling); job queues (jobs-cron, job-lanes-outbox); before/after mutation diffs (AuditLog, audit-soft-delete).

### Class `app-events`: emitAppEvent side-effect bus: handlers, handoffs to email/ws/observe, commit deferral

**Job: trigger a side effect (email, notification, job, push) after a domain write** (Triggering side effects: emitAppEvent vs db.onCommit vs enqueueJob vs direct sends) — docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md § Purpose and execution, § Handler and handoff contracts; COMMUNICATIONS.md § Send Pipeline

*Said as:* "send an email or notification after this write", "do something once the transaction commits", "I'll call the email service right after saving", "queue the heavy work from the event", "where does this side effect belong"

| Member | Use when | Not when (use instead) |
|---|---|---|
| **emitAppEvent** | any email, SMS, analytics, notification or WebSocket push from business logic; deferred to commit | never call those services directly |
| **makeAppEvent** | define an event's handler (cbs + handoffs), registered in the handlers index | emitting (use emitAppEvent) |
| **db.onCommit** | other work that must run only after the txn commits | side effects of a business write (use emitAppEvent, which defers itself) |
| **enqueueJob (jobs-cron)** | heavy or retryable work, enqueued from an event cb | inline in the event handler |
| **sendEmail (email-delivery)** | plans recipients from an EmailHandoff, then enqueues deliverEmail | never enqueue by hand with recipients (emit with an EmailHandoff) |
| **deliverEmail (email-delivery)** | the per-recipient provider send | never enqueue directly (sendEmail does) |
| **AppEvent** | the stored event stream for side effects | before/after mutation diffs (AuditLog) |
| *inline call, no job* | light, best-effort, idempotent work after commit: a makeAppEvent cb runs inline, each task isolated by db.parallel allSettled; observation upserts AppEvent directly and is not a separate BullMQ job (APP_EVENTS.md § Purpose and execution, § Observe pipeline) | heavy or retryable work (enqueueJob from the event cb); a direct email/SMS/analytics call (always an app-event handoff); in tests enqueueJob already runs the handler inline |
| *no event for model webhooks* | a model's mutations should notify webhook subscribers: add it to webhookEnabledModels; the webhooks hook enqueues sendWebhook on commit (HOOKS.md § Webhooks › Enabling Webhooks for a Model) | named domain side effects (emitAppEvent); never an event cb that looks up subscriptions and enqueues deliveries |

**Job: push a realtime update from the server to connected clients** (WebSocket handoffs: sendToChannel vs sendToUser vs streamAppend vs refetch) — docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md § WebSocket handoffs; WEBSOCKETS.md § Publishing a refetch, § Data streams

*Said as:* "push a live update to connected clients", "tell the browser to refetch this list", "notify everyone watching this channel", "update one user's open tabs", "send the row change down the stream"

| Member | Use when | Not when (use instead) |
|---|---|---|
| **sendToChannel (ws-streams)** | deliver to a channel's subscribers | a specific user's sockets (use sendToUser); data streams (use streamAppend) |
| **sendToUser (ws-streams)** | deliver to one user's sockets | channel subscribers (use sendToChannel) |
| **streamAppend (ws-streams)** | every stream handoff (branded; built from STREAM_DEFINITIONS) | query invalidation (use refetch); never a hand-built { kind: 'stream' } |
| **refetch (ws-streams)** | tell clients to invalidate a query | row-level changes (use streamAppend) |
| **routeRow (ws-streams)** | shape an upsert payload by the route's responseSchema | never pass a raw Prisma row |

### Class `webhooks`: Outbound webhooks: subscriptions, signing, delivery jobs, SSRF-safe fetch

**Job: decide which model changes emit webhooks and to whom** (Webhook registries: webhookEnabledModels vs webhookOwnerAllowedModels vs webhookModelSubscribers vs webhookRelatedModels) — docs/claude/HOOKS.md § Webhooks (Enabling Webhooks for a Model, Related Models); catalog registries/webhook

*Said as:* "make changes to this model notify subscribers", "which models can an owner subscribe to", "a child change should fire the parent's webhook", "turn on webhooks for a model", "I'll write a hook that enqueues deliveries for this model"

| Member | Use when | Not when (use instead) |
|---|---|---|
| **webhookEnabledModels** | make a model's mutations emit webhooks (add it here) | never a custom hook or event cb that enqueues deliveries |
| **webhookOwnerAllowedModels** | allow an owner to subscribe to a model (edit here) | starting from the changed model (use webhookModelSubscribers) |
| **webhookModelSubscribers** | inverse lookup: from a changed model to owners | permitting subscriptions (use webhookOwnerAllowedModels) |
| **webhookRelatedModels** | a child change fires the parent's webhook | never extra code to fire the parent |

**Job: deliver webhooks and validate subscriber URLs** (Delivery and URL safety: sendWebhook vs validateWebhookUrl vs webhookUrlSchema) — catalog sendWebhook, validateWebhookUrl, webhookUrlSchema; HOOKS.md § Webhooks

*Said as:* "deliver the webhook to the subscriber", "make sure the URL isn't pointing at something internal", "where are the subscription config and the delivery history", "I'll post to the receiver from the controller", "sign and send the payload"

| Member | Use when | Not when (use instead) |
|---|---|---|
| **sendWebhook** | the delivery job, enqueued per subscription by the webhook hook | never fetch subscriber URLs from a controller, hook or event cb |
| **validateWebhookUrl** | any user-supplied target URL outside zod | request bodies (use webhookUrlSchema) |
| **webhookUrlSchema** | schema-level URL check on subscription bodies | outside zod parsing (use validateWebhookUrl) |
| **WebhookSubscription** | the subscriber endpoint config (polymorphic owner) | delivery history (use WebhookEvent) |
| **WebhookEvent** | delivery history per subscription | endpoint config (use WebhookSubscription) |

- **WebhookEvent** · model `packages/db/prisma/schema/webhookEvent.prisma` · in docs: docs/claude/HOOKS.md § Webhooks; FEATURES.md § Webhooks: Delivery history per subscription: use this; subscriber endpoint config: WebhookSubscription instead.
  - *Said as:* "the delivery history for a subscription", "record every terminal failure so delivery health stays visible", "I'll log webhook failures and move on", "what was sent, when, and whether it succeeded", "show the receiver's recent deliveries in the management UI"
- **WebhookSubscription** · model `packages/db/prisma/schema/webhookSubscription.prisma` · in docs: docs/claude/HOOKS.md § Application Hooks; docs/claude/HOOKS.md § False Polymorphism: Owner is polymorphic via ownerModel plus one of userId/organizationId/spaceId; unique per owner, model and url.
  - *Said as:* "a receiver signed up to be told when this model changes", "the endpoint config an owner registers for a model", "I'll build a custom pipeline to push changes to the CRM", "I'll hand-roll subscription, trigger, loop-break and retry machinery", "outbound webhooks to a URL the owner gave us", "unique per owner, model and URL"
- **registerWebhookSubscriptionUrlHook** · primitive `apps/api/src/hooks/webhookSubscriptionUrl/hook.ts#registerWebhookSubscriptionUrlHook`: register a db hook that checks WebhookSubscription URL writes

- **sendWebhook** · primitive `apps/api/src/jobs/handlers/sendWebhook.ts#sendWebhook` · in docs: docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Webhooks; docs/claude/HOOKS.md § Webhooks: Normally enqueued by the webhook hook per subscription; don't call providers or fetch directly.

  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* fetch()/POST to subscriber URLs from a controller, hook or app-event cb, with signing and retry hand-rolled (catalog sendWebhook; docs/claude/HOOKS.md § Webhooks, How It Works)

  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* hand-rolled localhost/10.x/169.254 checks, or no check at all, before fetching a user-supplied URL (catalog validateWebhookUrl ("Use this for any user-supplied target URL"))
- **webhookEnabledModels** · primitive `packages/db/src/registries/webhook/enabledModels.ts#webhookEnabledModels` · in docs: docs/claude/HOOKS.md § Webhooks: list models whose mutations emit outbound webhooks (currently CustomerRef)

  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a custom after-mutation hook or app-event cb that looks up subscriptions and enqueues deliveries for a model, instead of adding the model to webhookEnabledModels (docs/claude/HOOKS.md § Webhooks, Enabling Webhooks for a Model)

  - *Said as:* "disable the subscription after it keeps failing", "five failures in a row and it turns off", "I'll add a failure counter and a disabled flag", "repeated rejections for one record poison the record instead"

## 4. The specifics, in full

### 4a. Doc sections

Each unit is the doc section verbatim, with its headings shifted down two levels. A source line above it gives the path, the section and the doc's H1.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#purpose-and-execution -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Purpose and execution (in "App Events")

#### Purpose and execution

Business logic never calls email, SMS, analytics, or notification services directly; every side
effect goes through an app event. Direct calls couple every controller to every channel and put
provider outages in the request path. Nothing synchronous hits an external service.

Business write paths emit events; handlers select side effects. Email delivery runs in jobs,
WebSocket handoffs use Redis pub/sub, and observation records the event envelope. This keeps
delivery logic out of controllers and lets each consumer evolve independently.

`emitAppEvent(name, data)` creates a UUIDv7 envelope with actor provenance from
`auditActorContext` and dispatches the registered handler. Inside `db.txn()`, execution is
registered with `db.onCommit`; outside a transaction, the handler is awaited immediately.

`makeAppEvent` executes observation, each email/WebSocket handoff, and each callback through
`db.parallel(tasks, { resolution: 'allSettled' })`. Each task gets its own database async scope.
A failed task does not prevent siblings from running; collected failures are thrown after
settlement. This isolation matters when a callback starts a transaction or runs a test-mode job
inline while the observe adapter also writes.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#emitting-and-registering-events -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Emitting and registering events (in "App Events")

#### Emitting and registering events

```typescript
import { emitAppEvent } from '#/appEvents';

await emitAppEvent('user.verificationRequested', {
  userId: user.id,
  verificationUrl,
});
```

Event names and payload types are declared in `apps/api/src/appEvents/handlers/index.ts`.
Add the payload, `AppEventName` entry and handler registration there. Each handler lives in
its feature folder and is constructed with `makeAppEvent`:

```typescript
export const userVerificationRequested = makeAppEvent<UserVerificationRequestedPayload>({
  email: (data) => [{
    template: 'email-verification',
    data: { userId: data.userId, verificationUrl: data.verificationUrl },
  }],
});
```

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#handler-and-handoff-contracts -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Handler and handoff contracts (in "App Events")

#### Handler and handoff contracts

```typescript
type EmailHandoff = {
  template: string;
  data: Record<string, unknown>;
};

type WSChannelsHandoff = {
  kind: 'channels';
  target: { channels: string[] };
  message: { data: Record<string, unknown> };
};

type WSUsersHandoff = {
  kind: 'users';
  target: { userIds: string[] };
  message: { data: Record<string, unknown> };
};

type WSStreamAppendHandoff = {
  kind: 'stream';
  target: { stream: string; userIds?: string[] };
  append: { type: string; payload: unknown };
};

type WSHandoff = WSChannelsHandoff | WSUsersHandoff | WSStreamAppendHandoff;

type AppEventHandlerDefinition<T> = {
  email?: (data: T) => EmailHandoff[] | null;
  websocket?: (data: T) => WSHandoff[] | null;
  cb?: Array<(data: T) => Promise<void> | void>;
};
```

There is no per-handler `observe` selector: the complete envelope is always sent to the
observe registry. Sender, recipients and delivery policy are defined by the email registry,
not supplied as `to`/`cc`/`bcc` on an event's email handoff.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#email-pipeline -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Email pipeline (in "App Events")

#### Email pipeline

`deliverEmailHandoffs` enqueues `sendEmail` with the template, event name and binding data,
using a deterministic planner job ID. The registry entry in `apps/api/src/lib/email/registry.ts`
defines the entity lens, sender, recipient rules, data lens and render policy.

The planner resolves entity/sender/template ownership, hydrates recipients through the
owner-scoped recipient lens, and creates or reuses a `CommunicationLog` row per recipient
using its idempotency key. It then enqueues `deliverEmail`. Delivery settles the template and
its component versions, applies contact preferences and address verification, renders and
sends, and records the result. See [COMMUNICATIONS.md](COMMUNICATIONS.md#planner-sendemail)
for the complete planner/delivery and degraded-rule behavior.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#websocket-handoffs -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § WebSocket handoffs (in "App Events")

#### WebSocket handoffs

Channel-targeted example, from `segmentMembersAdded`:

```typescript
websocket: (data) => [{
  target: { channels: [WS_CHANNELS.segmentReadManySegmentMembers.name(data.segmentId)] },
  message: { data: refetch({ _id: 'segmentReadManySegmentMembers', path: { id: data.segmentId } }) },
}],
```

`deliverWSHandoffs` sends a message handoff through `sendToChannel` or `sendToUser`, and a
stream handoff through `appendToStream`. The frontend handles query-refetch hints and
data-stream actions. New payload kinds require their own consumer and recovery design.
Subscription and stream-open checks use the underlying authorized route; see
[WEBSOCKETS.md](WEBSOCKETS.md).

Stream handoffs are never built by hand. `streamAppend` (`apps/api/src/appEvents/streamAppend.ts`)
takes a shared stream definition, its params, an op and a payload. The op must be one the
definition's kind defines (`list`: `upsert`, `remove`; `log`: `append`), the payload is typed by
that op, and the options argument carries `revive` (upserts only: may restore a removed row) and,
for a `perRecipient` definition, the required recipient `userIds`. An upsert row must come from
`routeRow(route, value)`, which parses it with the route's own `responseSchema` exactly as the
route's response is. From the
contact handlers (the scaffolding example stream):

```typescript
websocket: ({ contact }) => organizationContactRemove(contact),

// organizationContactRemove:
streamAppend(STREAM_DEFINITIONS.organizationReadManyContacts, { id: contact.organizationId }, 'remove', {
  id: contact.id,
});
```

A `shared` stream's append goes to every connection holding the stream, so it has to match the
shape of the route's response for every caller. `appendToStream` publishes each stream's appends
through a per-stream `createSerializedQueue`, so one instance emits them in order. See
[WEBSOCKETS.md](WEBSOCKETS.md#data-streams).

Revoking access (membership, role or token removal) does not yet emit an app event that closes
streams immediately; the periodic re-authorization in
[WEBSOCKETS.md](WEBSOCKETS.md#authorization-and-re-authorization) closes them within one
interval.

Segments also publish member-side `customerRef.segmentsAdded` / `customerRef.segmentsRemoved`
events. For User customers those target the user's sockets with a membership-query refetch.
See [SEGMENTS.md](SEGMENTS.md#events-and-email-integration).

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#observe-pipeline -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Observe pipeline (in "App Events")

#### Observe pipeline

The envelope contains `id`, `name`, `actor` and `data`. Observation broadcasts it through
`observeRegistry` to the structured log and database adapters. The database adapter directly
upserts `AppEvent` by envelope ID. This is idempotent, best-effort observation, not a durable
retry queue. The event ID encodes emit time; observation is not a separate BullMQ job.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#inquiry-events -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Inquiry events (in "App Events")

#### Inquiry events

Inquiry-specific definitions live under `apps/api/src/modules/inquiry/handlers/<type>/appEvents.ts`.
The central inquiry event handlers delegate to those definitions. For example, the
organization-invitation `sent` definition selects `inquiry-invite-organization-user` with
`{ inquiryId }` bindings and publishes an `inquiryRead` refetch. Its `resolved` definition
publishes the refetch. Use the shared handoff contracts for both.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#source-map-and-pending-consumers -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Source map and pending consumers (in "App Events")

#### Source map and pending consumers

- `apps/api/src/appEvents/emit.ts`: typed emit, actor envelope and commit deferral.
- `apps/api/src/appEvents/makeAppEvent.ts`: task isolation and failure aggregation.
- `apps/api/src/appEvents/types.ts`: envelope, handoffs and handler definition.
- `apps/api/src/appEvents/channels/`: email and WebSocket delivery bridges.
- `apps/api/src/appEvents/handlers/`: business-event handlers and the registry.
- `apps/api/src/lib/observe.ts`: observation adapters.
- `apps/api/src/jobs/handlers/sendEmail.ts`, `deliverEmail.ts`: email planner and delivery.

Feature flags and persisted in-app notifications remain future consumers. Registering an event
handler does not prove that a business writer emits the event; the Segments documentation
lists the reconciliation events still waiting for production write paths.

<!-- unit doc:AI/ENTRYPOINT.md#6-app-events-side-effects -->
**Source:** `AI/ENTRYPOINT.md` § 6. App Events & Side Effects (in "AI ENTRYPOINT")

#### 6. App Events & Side Effects

Business logic NEVER calls email, SMS, analytics, or notification services directly. All side effects go through `emitAppEvent`. Read `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` before modifying the event system.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#webhooks -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md` § Webhooks (in "Communications")

#### Webhooks

Existing webhook system. See [HOOKS.md](HOOKS.md) for webhook delivery.

```typescript
// Current: webhooks sent via sendWebhook job
db.onCommit(() => enqueue('sendWebhook', { ... }));
```

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/HOOKS.md#webhooks -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/HOOKS.md` § Webhooks (in "Hooks")

#### Webhooks

Automatic webhook delivery on database mutations.

##### Enabling Webhooks for a Model

```typescript
// packages/db/src/registries/webhook/enabledModels.ts
export const webhookEnabledModels: WebhookModel[] = [
  WebhookModel.CustomerRef,
];
```

##### How It Works

1. DB mutation triggers `webhookDelivery` hook (after commit)
2. Hook finds active subscriptions for the model
3. Enqueues `sendWebhook` job for each subscription
4. Job signs payload with RSA-SHA256 and delivers

##### Webhook Payload

```typescript
{
  model: 'User',
  action: 'create' | 'update' | 'delete',
  resourceId: '...',
  data: { ...fields },
  previousData: { ...fields },  // For updates only
  timestamp: '2024-01-15T12:00:00.000Z'
}
```

Headers: `Content-Type: application/json`, `X-Webhook-Signature: <base64>`

##### Circuit Breaker

After 5 consecutive failures, subscription auto-disables:

```typescript
const FAILURE_THRESHOLD = 5;
// If last 5 events all failed → isActive = false
```

##### Poisoned Records

On a subscription with an `integrationId`, one record the receiver keeps rejecting is poisoned
instead of tripping the circuit. A rejection is an `error` event with `httpStatus` 400 or 422
(`RECORD_REJECTION` in `sendWebhook.ts`). Other terminal failures such as redirects, 401, 403 or 429
do not count, and neither does `unreachable`. When a record has 3 rejections since its own last
success, and some other record has delivered since the first of them, `poisonIntegrationRecord`
stamps `IntegrationRecord.poisonedAt`. Later deliveries of that record are skipped before signing,
with no `WebhookEvent` and nothing fed to the circuit. Nothing clears the stamp yet. See
`tickets/INFRA-032-webhook-poisoned-records.md`.

##### Ignored Fields

`HOOK_IGNORE_FIELDS` is the **shared** ignore registry — used by audit, cache, webhooks, and the generic `isNoOpUpdate`. Any field listed here is:

1. **Excluded from payload** - never sent to webhook subscribers
2. **Stripped before audit diff** - changes don't produce AuditLog entries
3. **Treated as a no-op** - updates that only touch ignored fields skip the cache/webhook/audit hooks

```typescript
// packages/db/src/registries/ignoreFields.ts
const HOOK_IGNORE_FIELDS_BASE: Record<string, string[]> = {
  _global: ['updatedAt'],      // Always ignored for all models
  User: ['lastLoginAt'],       // Login timestamp not meaningful
  Token: ['lastUsedAt'],       // Token usage timestamp not meaningful
};

// Auto-composes from encryption + orderedList registries so encrypted column
// triplets (encryptedX / encryptedXMetadata / encryptedXKeyVersion) and
// ordered-list position fields don't need to be re-listed per model.
export const HOOK_IGNORE_FIELDS = buildHookIgnoreFields();
```

Use cases:
- **Timestamps** (`updatedAt`, `lastUsedAt`) - noisy, not meaningful
- **Sensitive data** (encrypted blobs) - auto-composed from encryption registry
- **Presentation-only state** (ordered-list `position`) - auto-composed from orderedList registry; the `orderedList` hook owns cache invalidation for ordering cascades (see [Ordered List](#ordered-list))

##### Related Models

Child models can trigger parent webhooks:

```typescript
// packages/db/src/registries/webhook/relatedModels.ts
export const webhookRelatedModels: Record<string, FlexibleRef[]> = {
  User: [{ model: 'CustomerRef', axis: 'customerModel', value: 'User' }],
};
```

---

<!-- unit doc:FEATURES.md#webhooks -->
**Source:** `FEATURES.md` § Webhooks (in "Template Features")

#### Webhooks

**Event-Driven Integration System** - Notify external systems when data changes. Organizations/spaces subscribe to events, receive RSA-SHA256-signed payloads. Automatic retries, delivery tracking, and async processing via job queue.

- ✅ **Webhook Subscriptions** - Organizations and spaces can subscribe to events (user.created, organization.updated, etc.). Each subscription has URL, events list, and active/inactive status. Payloads are signed with a server-held RSA private key (asymmetric); receivers verify with the published public key. False polymorphism pattern allows User/Organization/Space ownership

- ✅ **Event-Based Triggers** - Database hooks automatically fire webhook deliveries after successful mutations. Hook system ensures webhooks only sent after transaction commits. Events follow pattern: `{resource}.{action}` (user.created, token.deleted)

- ✅ **RSA Signature Verification** - Each webhook includes `x-webhook-signature` header with an RSA-SHA256 signature (base64). Signed with a server-held private key; receivers verify with the public key exposed at `/webhookSubscription/info`. Asymmetric — no shared secret to leak. Signed body includes a unix `timestamp` so receivers can reject replays. Prevents webhook spoofing and tampering

- ✅ **Async Delivery via Jobs** - Webhooks enqueued as BullMQ jobs on the shared `jobs` queue. Never blocks request processing. Failed deliveries retry automatically (3 attempts, exponential backoff). Webhook jobs run outside transaction to avoid timeouts

- ✅ **Delivery Tracking** - WebhookEvent model records every delivery attempt with status (pending, sent, failed), response code, response body, error message. Superadmins can inspect delivery history and debug integration issues

- ✅ **Automatic Cleanup** - Cron job removes old webhook events (90+ days) to prevent unbounded table growth. Configurable retention period

- ✅ **Superadmin Oversight** - Superadmin routes for viewing all subscriptions across organizations, inspecting delivery failures, manually retriggering failed deliveries

---

### 4b. Code entries

From the catalog (`.foundry/catalog/catalog.json`, extracted from the code). Each line: **name** `where` [kind] the job it does. Use: canonical usage.

#### Class `app-events`
- **AppEvent** `packages/db/prisma/schema/appEvent.prisma` [model] record emitted app events with actor, source and JSON payload Use: db.appEvent.findMany({ where: { name } })
- **emitAppEvent** `apps/api/src/appEvents/emit.ts#emitAppEvent` [primitive] trigger all side effects of a domain change, deferred until transaction commit Use: await emitAppEvent('contactCreated', { contact })
- **makeAppEvent** `apps/api/src/appEvents/makeAppEvent.ts#makeAppEvent` [primitive] define an app event handler running observation, email, WebSocket and callbacks in isolation Use: export const myEvent = makeAppEvent<MyPayload>({ email: (d) => [...], cb: [async (d) => {...}] });

#### Class `webhooks`
- **WebhookEvent** `packages/db/prisma/schema/webhookEvent.prisma` [model] record each outbound webhook delivery attempt with status, payload and HTTP result Use: db.webhookEvent.findMany({ where: { webhookSubscriptionId, status } })
- **WebhookSubscription** `packages/db/prisma/schema/webhookSubscription.prisma` [model] register a user, organization or space URL to receive webhooks for a model Use: db.webhookSubscription.create({ data: { model, url, ownerModel, organizationId } })
- **registerWebhookSubscriptionUrlHook** `apps/api/src/hooks/webhookSubscriptionUrl/hook.ts#registerWebhookSubscriptionUrlHook` [primitive] register a db hook that checks WebhookSubscription URL writes Use: registerWebhookSubscriptionUrlHook(); // at startup with the other db hooks
- **sendWebhook** `apps/api/src/jobs/handlers/sendWebhook.ts#sendWebhook` [primitive] deliver one webhook event to one subscription Use: enqueue sendWebhook with { subscriptionId, action, resourceId, data, timestamp }
- **validateWebhookUrl** `apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/validators/validateWebhookUrl.ts#validateWebhookUrl` [primitive] reject unsafe user-supplied webhook URLs before sending, throwing an app error Use: validateWebhookUrl(url); // optional { enforce: false }
- **webhookEnabledModels** `packages/db/src/registries/webhook/enabledModels.ts#webhookEnabledModels` [primitive] list models whose mutations emit outbound webhooks (currently CustomerRef) Use: webhookEnabledModels.includes(WebhookModel.CustomerRef)
- **webhookModelSubscribers** `packages/db/src/registries/webhook/ownerAllowedModels.ts#webhookModelSubscribers` [primitive] look up which owner models may subscribe to webhooks for a given model Use: webhookModelSubscribers[WebhookModel.CustomerRef] // owner models allowed
- **webhookOwnerAllowedModels** `packages/db/src/registries/webhook/ownerAllowedModels.ts#webhookOwnerAllowedModels` [primitive] declare which models each webhook owner (User, Organization, Space) may subscribe to Use: webhookOwnerAllowedModels[WebhookOwnerModel.Organization]
- **webhookRelatedModels** `packages/db/src/registries/webhook/relatedModels.ts#webhookRelatedModels` [primitive] map an owner model to related records whose changes fire its webhooks Use: webhookRelatedModels[modelName] // FlexibleRef[] with model, axis, value
- **webhookUrlSchema** `apps/api/src/modules/webhookSubscription/schemas/webhookSubscriptionSchemas.ts#webhookUrlSchema` [primitive] reject unsafe webhook target URLs at schema validation via validateWebhookUrl Use: url: webhookUrlSchema
- **apps/api/src/modules/webhookSubscription** `apps/api/src/modules/webhookSubscription` [system] read, update, delete webhook subscriptions and list all as superadmin Use: apps/api/src/modules/webhookSubscription — webhookSubscriptionRead / webhookSubscriptionUpdate
